questions.question: What does the CSS box model refer to?
options: Properties that control the layout of rectangular boxes (width, height, margin, padding, border, box-sizing)
A method for organizing CSS files
questions.explanation: The box model refers to properties that control the layout of rectangular boxes, including width, height, margin, padding, border, and box-sizing. Every element in web design is a rectangular box.

questions.question: What is the space INSIDE an element, between the content and the border?
questions.explanation: Padding is the space inside an element, between the content and the border. It's part of the box model.

questions.question: What is the space OUTSIDE an element, between the element and other elements?
questions.explanation: Margin is the space outside an element, between the element and other elements. It's part of the box model.

questions.question: What does 'box-sizing: border-box' do?
options: It does not count padding and border in size calculations (padding and border are included in the width/height)
It removes all padding and borders
questions.explanation: 'box-sizing: border-box' means that padding and border are included in the width/height calculations. This is often preferred because it makes sizing more predictable.

questions.question: Which of the following is a valid way to set padding on all sides?
options: padding: 10px 10px 10px 10px; (but the first option is simpler)
questions.explanation: You can set padding with 'padding: 10px;' (applies to all sides) or 'padding: 10px 10px 10px 10px;' (top, right, bottom, left). The first option is simpler when all sides are the same.

questions.question: Which of the following properties can be set individually for each side?
questions.explanation: Both padding and margin can be set individually for each side. For example: padding-top, padding-right, padding-bottom, padding-left, and similarly for margin.

questions.question: What does 'vh' stand for in CSS units?
options: Viewport height (1% of the height of the browser window)
questions.explanation: 'vh' stands for viewport height - it's relative to 1% of the height of the browser window. For example, 'width: 10vh;' means 10% of the viewport height.

questions.question: What does 'vw' stand for in CSS units?
options: Viewport width (1% of the width of the browser window)
questions.explanation: 'vw' stands for viewport width - it's relative to 1% of the width of the browser window. For example, 'width: 30vw;' means 30% of the viewport width.
'vh' stands for viewport height. 'width: 50vh;' means the width will be 50% of the viewport (browser window) height. Note: using vh for width is less common than vw, but it's valid.

questions.question: What is the correct syntax for setting a border?
options: All of the above are valid, but the first is the most common order
questions.explanation: The border shorthand property can be written as 'border: style width color;' or 'border: width style color;'. The most common order is 'border: style width color;' like 'border: dotted 1px #CCC;'

questions.question: In the box model, what is the order of layers from inside to outside?
questions.explanation: From inside to outside, the box model layers are: Content (innermost), then Padding, then Border, then Margin (outermost).

questions.question: What happens if you set 'width: 100%;' on an element?
options: The element takes up 100% of the screen width
The element takes up 100% of its parent element's width
questions.explanation: Percentage units are relative to the parent element. 'width: 100%;' means the element will take up 100% of its parent element's width, not the screen width.
